name: BASE dark-matter searches
full_name: Baryon Antibaryon Symmetry Experiment — dark-matter programme
summary: BASE primarily tests matter–antimatter symmetry and also uses precision single-antiproton spin data to search for dark matter.
detection_principle: Frequency-domain analysis of a single antiproton's spin-flip frequency in a Penning trap searches for periodic spin-precession changes induced by an axion background.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2020 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Direct limits on the interaction of antiprotons with axion-like dark matter

lead_institutions: Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: Direct axion–antiproton interaction limits were established; this does not imply discovery of matter–antimatter asymmetry or dark matter.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
